title: Uamué language - Wikipedia
text: February 18, 2026 - Uamué (Wamoe), a.k.a. Huamoé, Uman, or Atikum, is an extinct language of Brazil that is too poorly attested to classify. The Pankararú language was historically spoken just to the south. It is also spelled Huamuê, Huamoi, Uame, Wamoé. Alternate names are Umã and Aticum (Atikum, Araticum).

title: List of unclassified languages of South America - Wikipedia
text: April 22, 2026 - The following purported languages of South America are listed as unclassified in either Campbell (2024), Loukotka (1968), Ethnologue, or Glottolog. Nearly all are extinct. It is likely that many of them were not actually distinct languages, only ethnic or regional names.

title: Uamué Language (UAM) – L1 & L2 Speakers, Status, Map, Endangered Level & Official Use | Ethnologue Free
text: Uamué is a dormant language of Brazil. It is an isolate that is not known to be related to any other language. The language is no longer used as a first language by any remaining members of the ethnic community.
